track: shim (PDA-first entry behind an RA firewall)
result: KILL: notes and tools only, no source change proposed. Volatile/manual-slot firewalls decouple the protected region from the PDA-first entry (pf9v+F reproduces main+F there) but re-basin it on main too (main+F -53..-680); identity intrinsics (ptp, llvm.ptr.annotation) are near-transparent but do not decouple. Best pf9v+F T1+C1 is -150 (kill threshold -40).

kill_test.criterion: no firewall brings pf9v's T1+C1 within 40 tokens of main's while keeping E1 >= +20

tools.tools/cap.sh: crate copy + exact edits -> capraw pre-opt IR -> preslim -> fx (w17a06 exact slim oracle); deletes stale pump_recovered*.ll first and fails on error[E..] (the w17a08 copy silently reuses the previous variant's IR when a variant does not compile)
tools.tools/q.sh: two-wide capture queue with per-region rc.py tables against fx/${REF}
tools.tools/comp.py + tools/mk.py: named source-edit components (PDA-first k8/pf9v, volatile firewalls FT/FC/FS/FW/FJ/FE/FE2/FE4/F0, ptp PT/PC, ptr.annotation PAT/PAC/PAS/PAE4/PA0, manual hkx-tail slot MSst/MSstn/MSc1/MSc1n/MShk/MSt1cv/MSt1ep) composed into edit files
tools.tools/cdiff.py: two candidates side by side over an original window range (each aligned to the original)
tools.tools/rsize.py: candidate instruction count per original region
tools.tools/radiff2.py: greedy RA trace diff keyed by live-range start slot with a slot shift

findings: Firewall decoupling is real: a volatile ctx.accounts reload at a region head makes that region's allocation independent of the entry (T1: mFT -278 vs pFT -282; C1: mFC -77 vs pFC -76; sweep head: mFS -202 vs pFS -209).

No memory firewall is transparent: the fresh accounts vreg is a new short range allocated early by greedy (caller-saved r2 in the clone runs) where main has a late split piece of %0 (r8 in T1, r5 in C1); main+F loses 53 (manual slot, plain reads, C1) to 680 (after E1) tokens.
Identity intrinsics are not firewalls: ptp is deleted before ISel; llvm.ptr.annotation's COPY is coalesced into %0 (mPATC -13 on main but pPATC = pf9v in T1/C1).

The original reloads accounts from its spill slot -0x8d8 at all 8 C1 clone heads and at 3 T1 sites (creator_vault, pump_amm_event_authority, pump_amm program clones); main keeps C1's piece in r5 and T1's in r8 up to the event_authority clone; pf9v keeps r8 through the program clone, so the event_authority pointer and the copy-out scratch move (r8->r3, r1->r3).

Manual per-clone reloads from the hkx tail (-0x680) reproduce the original's C1 reload structure (rfj C1 +5) but cost ~53 naming tokens on main; the offset can never be -0x8d8 from source because the frame below the last IR alloca (mint, -0x6c0) is 33 backend 16 B sret-demotion temporaries.
pf9v's spill colours k6..k10 rotate because the curve-pointer spill interval SS#321 is shorter and heavier (1.375 vs 1.038); sscsim restoring main's rank gains only +5.

pf9v's C1 loss is partly inherited from T1: on aab087f the T1-only manual reloads (pMST, pMSTe) move pf9v's C1 from -49 to -24 without touching C1; on 53ec7fb pf9v itself is at C1 -24 (T1 still -235).
pf9v on the latest main 53ec7fb: 1960 @27432 vs main 2295 (E1 +27, T1 -235, C1 -24, W2 -21).

rejected_mechanisms: volatile ctx.accounts reload as an RA firewall at any region head (decouples, re-basins)
ptp passthrough / llvm.ptr.annotation on the accounts pointer as an RA firewall (no new live range survives)
manual accounts spill slot in the hkx tail with per-clone reloads (structure right, naming -53 on main)
hand-spill at -0x8d8 (frame bottom is backend sret-demotion temporaries; unreachable from source)
curve-pointer spill colour repair on pf9v (+5 only)
unresolved_residuals: PDA-first (E1 +27 exact, +24 rfj) costs ~360 M on every main tested, almost all register naming in T1/C1/W2 from the greedy re-basin.
A transparent firewall would need a fresh accounts range that greedy allocates late, like a split product of %0; source-level ranges are enqueued with the global bit and allocated early.
next_ideas: Do not retry PDA-first until the T1/C1 clone runs are robust on main itself (e.g. their accounts reload sites match the original's), so a re-basin no longer costs hundreds of tokens.

If a lane gets main's T1/C1 to reload accounts at the original's sites (8 in C1, 3 in T1), re-test pf9v+that: the manual-slot rows show the structure is reachable (C1 rfj +5) and pf9v's C1 loss is partly inherited from T1.
pFE4 (firewall after validate, 2004 @27392 on 4d09af4) and pPASMS (2029 @27456 on 53ec7fb) are the best PDA-first bases if someone wants to RA-tune the PDA-first basin with weight shims.
